audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Nehemiah 5 documents social crisis during wall-building and Nehemiah's economic reforms. Text preserves creditor-debtor conflict, vulnerability of daughters to enslavement, and Nehemiah's self-exaltation of personal honor. Verse 5 contains textual difficulty (יָדֵנוּ with negative); verse 7 shows textual variant (נשאים vs נֹשִׁים). No source-versification boundary adjustments needed.

verses.restored: Now there came a great cry of the people and their wives against their brothers, the Judeans.

familiar.text: And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.

notes.title: צַעֲקַת
notes.body: Organized outcry, not mere lamentation; suggests coordinated complaint, collective consciousness of injustice.

modern.text: About that time there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֨י צַעֲקַ֥ת הָעָ֛ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם גְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַיְּהוּדִֽים

verses.restored: For some were saying: 'Our sons and daughters—we are many. We must obtain grain so we can eat and live.'

familiar.text: For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters, are many: therefore we take up corn for them, that we may eat, and live.

modern.text: Some were saying, “We and our sons and daughters are numerous. We must get grain in order to eat and stay alive.”

original.text: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים בָּנֵ֥ינוּ וּבְנֹתֵ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן וְנֹאכְלָ֥ה וְנִחְיֶֽה

verses.restored: And some were saying: 'Our fields, our vineyards, and our houses—we are pledging them so we can get grain in the dearth.'

familiar.text: Some also there were that said, We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.

modern.text: Others were saying, “We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our homes to get grain during the famine.”

original.text: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים שְׂדֹתֵ֛ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֥ינוּ וּבָתֵּ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹרְבִ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן בָּרָעָֽב

verses.restored: And some were saying: 'We have borrowed money for the king's portion against our fields and vineyards.'

familiar.text: There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards.

modern.text: Still others were saying, “We have borrowed money to pay the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards.

original.text: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים לָוִ֥ינוּ כֶ֖סֶף לְמִדַּ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׂדֹתֵ֖ינוּ וּכְרָמֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: And now, our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, our children like their children; yet behold, we are subjecting our sons and our daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We have no power in our hands—our fields and our vineyards belong to others.

familiar.text: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.

notes.title: textual anomaly
notes.body: Phrase 'there is no power in our hands' (אֵין לְאֵל יָדֵנוּ) is grammatically marked; may indicate textual damage or archaic construction.

modern.text: We and our children are just like our countrymen and their children, yet we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved, but we are powerless to redeem them because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּבְשַׂ֤ר אַחֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּשָׂרֵ֔נוּ כִּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם בָּנֵ֑ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֣ה אֲנַ֣חְנוּ כֹ֠בְשִׁים אֶת בָּנֵ֨ינוּ וְאֶת בְּנֹתֵ֜ינוּ לַעֲבָדִ֗ים וְיֵ֨שׁ מִבְּנֹתֵ֤ינוּ נִכְבָּשׁוֹת֙ וְאֵ֣ין לְאֵ֣ל יָדֵ֔נוּ וּשְׂדֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ לַאֲחֵרִֽים

verses.restored: And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.

familiar.text: And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words.

modern.text: When I heard their outcry and these complaints, I became extremely angry,

original.text: וַיִּ֥חַר לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת זַֽעֲקָתָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: And my heart deliberated within me, and I contended with the nobles and the officials, saying to them: 'You—you are exacting a burden, each from his brother.' And I called together a great assembly against them.

familiar.text: Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.

notes.title: variant reading
notes.body: Verse 7 shows textual variant: קרי reads נֹשִׁים (exacting, participating in burden-taking); some sources show נשאים. Both preserve sense of unjust extraction.

modern.text: and after serious thought I rebuked the nobles and officials, saying, “You are exacting usury from your own brothers!” So I called a large assembly against them

original.text: וַיִּמָּלֵ֨ךְ לִבִּ֜י עָלַ֗י וָאָרִ֨יבָה֙ אֶת הַחֹרִ֣ים וְאֶת הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם מַשָּׁ֥א אִישׁ בְּאָחִ֖יו אַתֶּ֣ם נשאים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְהִלָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: And I said to them: 'We have redeemed our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations according to our ability, and you—you are selling your brothers, and they are sold to us?' And they were silent and found no word.

familiar.text: And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.

modern.text: and said, “We have done our best to buy back our Jewish brothers who were sold to foreigners, but now you are selling your own brothers, that they may be sold back to us!” But they remained silent, for they could find nothing to say.

original.text: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם אֲנַ֣חְנוּ קָ֠נִינוּ אֶת אַחֵ֨ינוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַנִּמְכָּרִ֤ים לַגּוֹיִם֙ כְּדֵ֣י בָ֔נוּ וְגַם אַתֶּ֛ם תִּמְכְּר֥וּ אֶת אֲחֵיכֶ֖ם וְנִמְכְּרוּ לָ֑נוּ וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹ֥א מָצְא֖וּ דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: I said further: 'Not good is the thing that you are doing. Ought you not to walk in fear of our God, away from the reproach of the nations, our enemies?'

familiar.text: Also I said, It is not good that ye do: ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies?

modern.text: So I continued, “What you are doing is not right. Shouldn’t you walk in the fear of our God to avoid the reproach of our foreign enemies?

original.text: ויאמר לֹא ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲל֞וֹא בְּיִרְאַ֤ת אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ תֵּלֵ֔כוּ מֵחֶרְפַּ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Moreover, I and my brothers and my servants—we are exacting interest from them in silver and grain. Let us let go of this interest.

familiar.text: I likewise, and my brethren, and my servants, might exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury.

modern.text: I, as well as my brothers and my servants, have been lending the people money and grain. Please, let us stop this usury.

original.text: וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אַחַ֣י וּנְעָרַ֔י נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶ֖ם כֶּ֣סֶף וְדָגָ֑ן נַֽעַזְבָה נָּ֖א אֶת הַמַּשָּׁ֥א הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Return, I pray you, to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses; also the hundredth of the silver and the grain, the wine, and the oil that you are exacting from them.

familiar.text: Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, that ye exact of them.

modern.text: Please restore to them immediately their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the percentage of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been assessing them.”

original.text: הָשִׁיבוּ֩ נָ֨א לָהֶ֜ם כְּהַיּ֗וֹם שְׂדֹתֵיהֶ֛ם כַּרְמֵיהֶ֥ם זֵיתֵיהֶ֖ם וּבָתֵּיהֶ֑ם וּמְאַ֨ת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְהַדָּגָן֙ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶֽם

verses.restored: Then they said: 'We will return them, and we will demand nothing from them. So we will do as you say.' Then I called the priests and made them swear an oath to do according to this word.

familiar.text: Then said they, We will restore them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this promise.

modern.text: “We will restore it,” they replied, “and will require nothing more from them. We will do as you say.” So I summoned the priests and required of the nobles and officials an oath that they would do what they had promised.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ נָשִׁ֗יב וּמֵהֶם֙ לֹ֣א נְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כֵּ֣ן נַעֲשֶׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר וָאֶקְרָא֙ אֶת הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וָֽאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: I also shook out my lap and said: 'Thus may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this word—thus be he shaken out and emptied.' And all the assembly said 'Amen!' and praised YHWH. And the people did according to this word.

familiar.text: Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise, even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation said, Amen, and praised the LORD. And the people did according to this promise.

modern.text: I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, “May God likewise shake out of His house and possession every man who does not keep this promise. May such a man be shaken out and have nothing!” The whole assembly said, “Amen,” and they praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised. Nehemiah’s Generosity

original.text: גַּם חָצְנִ֣י נָעַ֗רְתִּי וָֽאֹמְרָ֡ה כָּ֣כָה יְנַעֵ֪ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֟ים אֶת כָּל הָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא יָקִ֜ים אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּיתוֹ֙ וּמִ֣יגִיע֔וֹ וְכָ֛כָה יִהְיֶ֥ה נָע֖וּר וָרֵ֑ק וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֜ל אָמֵ֗ן וַֽיְהַלְלוּ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָעָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Moreover, from the day when I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, that is, twelve years—I and my brothers did not eat the bread of the governor.

familiar.text: Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even unto the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor.

modern.text: Furthermore, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from his twentieth year until his thirty-second year (twelve years total), neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

original.text: גַּ֞ם מִיּ֣וֹם אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י לִהְי֣וֹת פֶּחָם֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָה֒ מִשְּׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֗ים וְ֠עַד שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֣סְתְּא הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁנִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה אֲנִ֣י וְאַחַ֔י לֶ֥חֶם הַפֶּ֖חָה לֹ֥א אָכַֽלְתִּי

verses.restored: But the former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them bread and wine besides forty shekels of silver; moreover their servants bore rule over the people. But I did not do so because of the fear of God.

familiar.text: But the former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people, and had taken of them bread and wine, beside forty shekels of silver; yea, even their servants bare rule over the people: but so did not I, because of the fear of God.

modern.text: The governors before me had heavily burdened the people, taking from them bread and wine plus forty shekels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people, but I did not do this because of my fear of God.

original.text: וְהַפַּחוֹת֩ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר לְפָנַ֜י הִכְבִּ֣ידוּ עַל הָעָ֗ם וַיִּקְח֨וּ מֵהֶ֜ם בְּלֶ֤חֶם וָיַ֨יִן֙ אַחַר֙ כֶּֽסֶף שְׁקָלִ֣ים אַרְבָּעִ֔ים גַּ֥ם נַעֲרֵיהֶ֖ם שָׁלְט֣וּ עַל הָעָ֑ם וַאֲנִי֙ לֹא עָשִׂ֣יתִי כֵ֔ן מִפְּנֵ֖י יִרְאַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Moreover, in the work of this wall I was strong, and we did not acquire land; and all my servants were gathered there unto the work.

familiar.text: Yea, also I continued in the work of this wall, neither bought we any land: and all my servants were gathered thither unto the work.

modern.text: Instead, I devoted myself to the construction of the wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any land.

original.text: וְ֠גַם בִּמְלֶ֜אכֶת הַחוֹמָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ הֶחֱזַ֔קְתִּי וְשָׂדֶ֖ה לֹ֣א קָנִ֑ינוּ וְכָל נְעָרַ֔י קְבוּצִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם עַל הַמְּלָאכָֽה

verses.restored: Moreover, one hundred fifty of the Judeans and the officials sat at my table, besides those coming to us from the nations round about us.

familiar.text: Moreover there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the Jews and rulers, beside those that came unto us from among the heathen that are about us.

modern.text: There were 150 Jews and officials at my table, besides the guests from the surrounding nations.

original.text: וְהַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֜ים מֵאָ֧ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהַבָּאִ֥ים אֵלֵ֛ינוּ מִן הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתֵ֖ינוּ עַל שֻׁלְחָנִֽי

verses.restored: Now what was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me; and in every ten days all manner of wine was brought. Yet despite all this I did not demand the bread of the governor, because the labor was heavy upon this people.

familiar.text: Now that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine: yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the bondage was heavy upon this people.

modern.text: Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and some fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. But I did not demand the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on the people was so heavy.

original.text: וַאֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֗ד שׁ֣וֹר אֶחָ֞ד צֹ֠אן שֵׁשׁ בְּרֻר֤וֹת וְצִפֳּרִים֙ נַֽעֲשׂוּ לִ֔י וּבֵ֨ין עֲשֶׂ֧רֶת יָמִ֛ים בְּכָל יַ֖יִן לְהַרְבֵּ֑ה וְעִם זֶ֗ה לֶ֤חֶם הַפֶּחָה֙ לֹ֣א בִקַּ֔שְׁתִּי כִּֽי כָֽבְדָ֥ה הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Remember me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.

familiar.text: Think upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.

modern.text: Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.

original.text: זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה

translation_notes: צַעֲקַת (cry/outcry) captures organized complaint, not mere weeping; feminine suggests collective voice.
Verse 5: יָדֵנוּ ('power in our hands') appears grammatically anomalous in negative construction; preserved as textual marker.
Verse 7: נֹשִׁים (exacting, burdensome) reads as present participle; textual variant נשאים in some sources.
Verse 13: Shaking-the-fold gesture (חׇצְנִי נָעַרְתִּי) is ancient summons formula, covenantal threat.
Verse 19: Solo final note by Nehemiah, no response; stands distinct from verse 13's collective Amen.
Throughout: עבדים (slavery, not servitude) and משא (exacted interest/burden) preserve economic coercion language.
safety_note: Chapter presents debt-slavery, exploitation of daughters, coerced labor, and social stratification as political facts requiring redress, not moral instruction. Nehemiah's self-commemoration (vv. 14-19) frames elite honor via abstention rather than structural justice; modern readers should not mistake this as sufficient economic reform.
source_witness_audit_flags: Verse 5: יָדֵנוּ phrase-boundary and negative grammatical form requires witness collation
Verse 7: Marginal variant נשאים vs. נֹשִׁים affects sense (bearing/burdensome vs. exacting)
